questions.title: Wallet Deposit Withdraw
questions.description:
An encapsulated wallet never exposes its money directly. Define a class Wallet with a private double field balance, a method deposit(double amount), a method withdraw(double amount) that subtracts only when amount <= balance and otherwise prints Insufficient funds, a method printBalance() that prints Balance: <balance with 2 decimals>, and a method getBalance(). In main, read n operations and apply them in order on one Wallet object: D amount deposits, W amount withdraws, P prints the current balance. After all operations print Final: <balance with 2 decimals> using getBalance().

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by an amount, or the letter P alone.

Output Format:
For every P print Balance: <balance with 2 decimals>; print Insufficient funds immediately for every rejected withdrawal; at the end print Final: <balance with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000
questions.input3: 7 D 100 W 40 P W 60 P D 1 P
questions.blacklist: public double balance, public int balance

questions.title: Student Marks Grade Private
questions.description:
A result portal keeps marks private and exposes only the computed grade. Define a class Student with a private int field marks, a method setMarks(int m) to store it, and a method grade() that returns A for marks >= 90, B for >= 75, C for >= 60, D for >= 40 and F otherwise. In main, read a student's name and marks, store the marks through setMarks, and print: <name> got grade <letter>.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated values: name marks (name is one word).

Output Format:
Print one line: <name> got grade <letter>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Private Helper Messages
questions.description:
Public methods often delegate the real work to private helpers, hiding the details from callers. Define a class Greeter with a private method buildMessage(String name, int number) that returns Hello, <name>! You are visitor number <number>. and a method greet(String name, int number) that prints whatever buildMessage returns. In main, read n names and, for each i from 1 to n, call greet with the name and i. The helper stays private; only greet is called from outside the class.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated names (single words).

Output Format:
Print n lines in order: Hello, <name>! You are visitor number <i>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= name length <= 50

questions.title: Age Setter Validation
questions.description:
A setter can refuse bad data instead of storing it. Define a class Person with a private int field age (default 0), a method setAge(int a) that stores a only when a >= 0 and otherwise prints Invalid age while keeping the previous value, and a method getAge(). In main, read n and then n candidate ages, call setAge for each in order, and finally print the current age using getAge().

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated integers (the candidate ages).

Output Format:
Print Invalid age for every rejected value (in order), then one final line with the current age.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000 <= candidate age <= 1000
questions.output1:
Invalid age
Invalid age
Invalid age
5

questions.title: Robots Created Counter
questions.description:
A robot factory wants to know how many robots exist at any moment. Define a class Robot with a static int field count starting at 0; every time a new Robot object is created the count increases by 1, because the counter belongs to the class itself and is shared by every object. In main, read n commands: NEW followed by a one-word name creates one Robot, COUNT prints the current value of the shared counter.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n commands, each written as NEW (followed by a one-word name) or COUNT.

Output Format:
Print one line for every COUNT command: the number of robots created so far.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
questions.sampleinput1: 6 NEW R2 COUNT NEW R5 COUNT NEW R9 COUNT
questions.input1: 4 COUNT NEW X NEW Y COUNT
questions.input3: 6 NEW A NEW B COUNT NEW C COUNT

questions.title: Thermostat Setter Validation
questions.description:
A smart thermostat accepts temperatures only inside a safe window. Define a class Thermostat with a private double field celsius starting at 20.0, a method setTemperature(double t) that stores t only when 10 <= t <= 35 and otherwise prints Out of range while keeping the old value, a method getCelsius(), and a method report() that prints two lines: Celsius: <celsius with 2 decimals> and Fahrenheit: <celsius * 9 / 5 + 32 with 2 decimals>. In main, read n operations: S t sets the temperature, P reports it.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter S followed by a number, or the letter P alone.

Output Format:
Print Out of range for every rejected S; for every P print the two lines described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -50 <= t <= 150

questions.title: Product Inventory Total Value
questions.description:
A storeroom holds many products, each with its own quantity and price. Define a class Product with fields name (String), quantity (int) and price (double), and a method stockValue() returning quantity * price. Read n products, create one Product object per record with new and keep them all in a Product[] array, then walk the array once and print each product's stock value, and finally the total value of the whole inventory.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n records, each written as name quantity price (name is one word).

Output Format:
Print n lines: <name> <stock value with 2 decimals> in input order, then one final line: Total: <total value with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= quantity <= 100000, 0 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Fleet Mileage Tracker
questions.description:
A delivery company watches every car's mileage. Define a class Car with a private int field distance and a private double field fuelUsed (both starting at 0), a method trip(int km, double litres) that adds to both, a method average() returning distance / fuelUsed (or 0.0 when distance is 0), and getters for both fields. Read n cars; each car has m trips given as km litres pairs. After reading everything, print one line per car: Car <i>: <distance> km, <average with 2 decimals> km/l, then the fleet summary: Fleet: <total km> km, <total km / total litres with 2 decimals> km/l.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by, for each car, the number m of trips and then m pairs of values km litres.

Output Format:
For each car in order print Car <i>: <km> km, <avg with 2 decimals> km/l; finally print Fleet: <km> km, <avg with 2 decimals> km/l.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= m <= 100, 0 <= km <= 100000, 0 <= litres <= 100000, total litres across the fleet > 0

questions.title: Bank Transaction Tally
questions.description:
A bank account keeps a private tally of every successful transaction. Define a class BankAccount with private fields balance, transactions, deposited and withdrawn (all starting at 0). deposit(double amount) always succeeds: it adds to balance, adds to deposited and increases transactions. withdraw(double amount) succeeds only when amount <= balance: it subtracts from balance, adds to withdrawn and increases transactions; otherwise it prints Rejected and changes nothing. Read n operations (D amount or W amount), apply them in order on one account object, then print the summary.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by an amount.

Output Format:
Print Rejected immediately for every failed withdrawal, then four summary lines: Balance: <2dp> / Transactions: <int> / Deposited: <2dp> / Withdrawn: <2dp>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Hospital Patient Manager
questions.description:
A hospital ward tracks its patients for one day. Define a class Patient with private fields name (String), age (int) and admitted (boolean), setters setName/setAge/setAdmitted and getters getName/getAge/isAdmitted; setName also marks the patient as admitted. Read n events: admit name age creates and stores a Patient object in a Patient[] array; discharge name finds the first still-admitted patient with that name and marks them discharged. At the end print four lines: Admitted: <number of admit events>, Discharged: <number of successful discharges>, Still in ward: <patients not discharged>, Oldest: <name of the oldest patient still admitted (age)> or Oldest: None when nobody remains.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n events, each written as admit name age or discharge name.

Output Format:
Four lines exactly as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= age <= 120, 1 <= name length <= 50; every discharge name was admitted earlier and not discharged before
